source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #303 (branch fix/301-op-shape-validation at head 9a3c4f2e2596f51eb9326b87cc198f858d6382d3 — per-op operand shape/count validation when decoding precompiled artifacts for #301: the generated op_registry shape table (OpShape and jump_target on every OpEntry, derived by tools/gen-op-registry.py) plus the validate_lowered shape/kind checks in precompiled.rs; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45458213378 and 45458228446 against the branch and pull-request run 45453767970, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #303 (#301, validate per-op operand shape/count when decoding precompiled artifacts). The PR extends the generated op registry with a per-op operand shape table (OpShape: Exact / Variadic / AnyOf, plus a jump_target flag on all 1,297 OpEntry rows, derived from the handlers themselves by tools/gen-op-registry.py) and adds shape/count and operand-kind validation to validate_lowered in the precompiled-module codec. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45458248974, 45458268050 and 45458286306 on main at 04bca9a8222d11a3d8db61204440e3d74a37c949): unmodified main produces byte-identical sizes to this branch on all 32 gated series and fails the gate on the same two series, so this PR's own contribution to every gated series is 0 B — the shape table and the validation code are not retained in any gated embedder configuration — and the delta against the checked-in baseline is entirely main-side baseline staleness. The checked-in baseline was measured on the PR #300 branch tree (3421c44: main 93581e8 plus PR #300) before PR #299 (precompiled-module codec, #196) merged; on the merged main (04bca9a) 26 of the 32 gated series differ from that baseline. Most library configurations shrink (in release, stripped file -1,000 B in core to -1,896 B in wasi, stripped .text -1,056 B to -1,952 B; in release-size, stripped file -32 B to -128 B and stripped .text -16 B to -80 B where they change); the baseline configuration is unchanged in both profiles. Only two series grow, each by 16 B: release-size core stripped .text (787,111 B to 787,127 B) and release-size wasi-threads stripped file (1,940,824 B to 1,940,840 B) — these two are the gate failures. The measured values coincide on every series with the re-baseline recorded for PR #302, which measured the same main. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release core-nosimd stripped file series at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,792 B), followed by the release component stripped file series at +9.77% (2,433,656 B to 2,671,528 B); both are slightly below the PR #300 cumulative figures because the merged main shrank against the PR #300 branch tree. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples.
